name: @pipeworx/mcp-congress-member-votes

tools.name: member_vote_positions
tools.description: ANSWERS "how did Rep. X vote on bill Y" / "what were X's last 20 votes" / "did X vote against the budget resolution" -- one member's recorded position (Yea, Nay, Present, Not Voting, or not on the roll) on roll calls, newest first -- House members from the U.S. House Clerk's roll-call votes, senators (chamber "senate") from the Congressional Record, where the Senate's roll calls are printed. Filter by `bill` (e.g. "H R 1"), `question_contains` (matched against question, bill number and description) or a roll range. Quorum calls, Speaker elections and Senate rolls whose record could not be derived are left out unless include_non_recorded is true. Every response names its chamber, congress, session, the last roll it covers and data_as_of. An unknown member or a Congress/session not held returns a named reason, never an empty list.

name.description: Surname as the Clerk prints it, e.g. "Pelosi"; combine with state when several members share it.

state.description: Two-letter state code to disambiguate a surname.

chamber.description: "house" (default) or "senate". The two chambers number their roll calls independently.

congress.description: Congress number, e.g. 119. Default: the newest held.

session.description: 1 or 2. Default: the newest held for the default Congress.

bill.description: Legislation number as the Clerk prints it, e.g. "H R 1", "H J RES 104", "S 2403" (punctuation and spacing ignored; exact match).

question_contains.description: Case-insensitive text to match in the vote question, bill number or description, e.g. "suspend the rules", "continuing appropriations".

include_non_recorded.description: Include quorum calls and Speaker-election rolls (default false).

tools.name: member_attendance_party_line
tools.description: ANSWERS "how many votes did Rep. X miss", "how often does X vote with their party", "party unity score" -- attendance and party-line share for ONE member (House, or a senator with chamber "senate") over a session (or a roll range), computed from the U.S. House Clerk's roll-call votes or, for the Senate, the Congressional Record's printed roll calls. Nothing is returned as a bare percentage: attendance gives its denominator (recorded roll calls the member was on the roll for; quorum calls, Speaker elections and Senate rolls that could not be derived are excluded and counted; rolls before the member was seated or after they left are excluded and counted -- absence from the roll is NOT treated as Not Voting) and splits yea/nay, present and Not Voting. Party line gives two figures, each with its own denominator and exclusions: share of yea/nay votes cast with the member's party majority (a strict majority of that party's yea/nay voters; ties excluded and counted), and party unity (only the roll calls where a majority of Democrats opposed a majority of Republicans). If a figure cannot be computed from the rolls in range (member on none, no party-splitting votes, independent) it is null with a stated reason, never 0% or 100%. Independents (including the Senate's two caucusing independents) have no D-versus-R majority to compare against, so their party-line figure is null with that reason.

name.description: Surname as the Clerk prints it, e.g. "Pelosi"; combine with state when several members share it.

state.description: Two-letter state code to disambiguate a surname.

chamber.description: "house" (default) or "senate". The two chambers number their roll calls independently.

congress.description: Congress number, e.g. 119. Default: the newest held.

session.description: 1 or 2. Default: the newest held for the default Congress.

from_roll.description: First roll number of the range (default 1).

to_roll.description: Last roll number of the range (default: last roll covered).

tools.name: roll_call_positions
tools.description: ANSWERS "who voted against roll call 100", "how did Texas Republicans split on roll 250", "how many Democrats voted Yea" -- every member's position on ONE roll call (House: the U.S. House Clerk's roll-call votes; Senate: the Congressional Record) with Yea/Nay/Present/Not Voting tallies by party. Pass party (D/R/I), state or position (yea/nay/present/not_voting) to list matching members; with none of these only the tallies and the roll's question, result and bill are returned. A roll number that does not exist in that session returns a named reason.

chamber.description: "house" (default) or "senate". The two chambers number their roll calls independently.

congress.description: Congress number, e.g. 119. Default: the newest held.

session.description: 1 or 2. Default: the newest held for the default Congress.

roll_number.description: Roll call number within the session, e.g. 100.

party.description: "D", "R" or "I" to list only that party.

state.description: Two-letter state code to list only that state's members.

instructions: @pipeworx/mcp-congress-member-votes forwards to the Pipeworx gateway and lists only the congress-member-votes pack's tools. Set PIPEWORX_META_TOOLS=1 to also list ask_pipeworx and the other gateway-wide tools.
